Proposition
[The gradient is normal to a regular level set]

↗ prop:regular-level-set-hypersurface-codim-one ↗ prop:regular-level-set-tangent-kernel ↗ def:gradient ↗ lem:gradient-orthogonal-kernel

Let $(M,g)$ be an $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold without boundary, $f\in C^\infty (M)$, and $c$ a regular value of $f$. If $\iota _c\colon f^{-1}(c)\hookrightarrow M$ is the inclusion, then for every $x_0\in f^{-1}(c)$ and $w\in T_{x_0}f^{-1}(c)$, \[ \left\langle \operatorname {grad}f|_{x_0},d(\iota _c)_{x_0}(w)\right\rangle =0. \] Thus $\operatorname {grad}f$ is normal to $f^{-1}(c)$.

Proof

↗ prop:regular-level-set-tangent-kernel ↗ lem:gradient-orthogonal-kernel \sketch Since $f\circ \iota _c$ is constant, the chain rule places $d(\iota _c)_{x_0}(w)$ in $\ker df_{x_0}$. Apply Lemma 5.

□
